insight.title: How the light beneath our feet shapes your world
insight.subtitle: A quiet dance of glass and pulses connecting every moment

sections.text: Our world is held together by threads of glass. Beneath the concrete and under the salt of the deep ocean, billions of tiny light pulses race through hair-thin fibers. They carry every message you send and every memory you share. While the sky feels like the source of magic, the true power lives in the silent ground.

Instead of slow electricity, we use the speed of pure light. Think of it as a Morse code made of flashes, bouncing off the inside of glass tubes without ever escaping. This sequence of brightness creates the digital world. It is a tireless, luminous river flowing quietly through the dark earth.

This invisible net turns your morning routine into a global symphony. When you tap a screen, you aren’t just touching glass; you are reaching across continents in an eye-blink. Distance has become a choice rather than a barrier. We have replaced the physical weight of paper with the weightless speed of the sun.
We are no longer limited by where we stand, but by where we choose to look.

news.title: Iran war hits Trump at home, March US inflation set for biggest jump since 2022, economists warn
news.description: US inflation is set for its sharpest monthly rise since 2022 as the Iran conflict drives a surge in fuel prices, raising stagflation risks and complicating policy choices for Donald Trump and the Federal Reserve
news.why: You will pay significantly more for fuel and basic household goods.

news.title: Oil back above $110 after expletive
news.description: Global oil prices have risen back above $110 (£83.38) a barrel after US President Donald Trump threatened to destroy critical infrastructure in Iran unless it allows ships to cross the Strait of Hormuz.
news.why: Higher transportation costs will likely lead to more expensive grocery bills.

news.title: Will RBI Hold Repo Rate Steady As Iran War, 'Super El Nino' Push Inflation Risks?
news.description: The central bank kept the repo rate unchanged in its August, October and February 2026 MPC meetings. The last rate cut was in December 2025.
news.why: Your monthly home loan and credit card payments could stay high.

news.title: Dollar steady as traders fret about escalating Iran war
news.description: The dollar remained steady as the yen neared 160 against the dollar amid escalating Iran conflict. President Trump issued a Tuesday deadline to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, threatening strikes on Iranian infrastructure. Investors are treating the situation as an oil-to-inflation-to-rates problem, favoring the dollar as a safe haven.
news.why: A strong dollar makes your international travel and imported goods expensive.

news.title: A War Pakistan Can’t Survive: Why Islamabad Is Pushing for Iran Ceasefire
news.description: The ongoing conflict in the Gulf, sparked by a US-Israeli offensive against Iran, has severely impacted Pakistan's economy, leading to high inflation and energy shortages. As Iran retaliates by targeting Gulf nations and closing the strategic Strait of Hormuz, Pakistan faces dire consequences that are becoming a question for its survival., Middle East, Times Now
news.why: Regional conflict may disrupt the production and delivery of items you buy.

news.title: Gold Falls as War Escalation and Jobs Data Reduce Rate-Cut Bets
news.description: Gold extended a decline as the escalating war in the Middle East heightened energy-supply and inflation risks, while a surprise drop in US jobless claims also reduced prospects for an interest-rate cut.
news.why: Higher interest rates mean you earn more on savings but borrow less.

news.title: Plus to push enterprise adoption of agentic AI
news.description: Alibaba has introduced Qwen3.6-Plus, a new artificial intelligence model designed to accelerate enterprise adoption of agentic AI, with enhanced capabilities in coding, multimodal reasoning, and autonomous task execution.
news.why: New automated tools could soon change how you perform office tasks.

news.title: Australia locks in another month's worth of fuel supply
news.description: Australia's Energy Minister Chris Bowen said the nation originally had supply until mid-April, but that had now been secured into May.
news.why: Supply shortages may soon lead to higher prices at your gas station.
